findings.title: Preserve the existing width/height downsize API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. Existing four-argument calls now treat the numeric height as `opts` and fail when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`; five-argument calls raise `ArgumentError`. Support both argument forms within one definition rather than silently removing the existing API.

findings.title: Keep attachment validation tied to its configured size limit
findings.body: The hardcoded 10 MB limit also applies to attachments, although the controller only downsizes images. Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are uploaded unchanged, while attachments permitted by a configured limit above 10 MB are now blocked. Relax the image limit without replacing the configured attachment limit.

findings.title: Identify animated GIFs independently of the tempfile suffix
findings.body: This passes the temporary path rather than the original filename to the optimizer. For an animated GIF backed by an extensionless multipart tempfile, `OptimizedImage.optimize` does not select its animated instructions because it checks whether the input path ends in `.gif`. It instead runs `convert` with the `[0]` frame selector and overwrites the uploaded original with a single frame, even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled. Determine the animation format from the original filename or file contents before resizing.

findings.title: Use supported resize dimensions for the animated GIF branch
findings.body: When the input path does end in `.gif` and animation is enabled, this percentage-based call reaches `resize_instructions_animated`, which generates `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects pixel dimensions in `WIDTHxHEIGHT` form, not a percentage, so the command fails. The controller ignores the result and repeats the same invalid command five times without reducing the oversized GIF. Calculate pixel dimensions for this branch or use an animation-preserving operation that supports percentage resizing.
